title: Canonical tensor-Hom adjunction formula for an immersion
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $s:S\hookrightarrow X$ be an immersion with a chosen factorization $S\xrightarrow{i}U\xrightarrow{j}X$, where $i$ is closed and $j$ is open [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $Rs_!=j_!i_*$, $Rs^!=Ri^!j^*$ and let $Rs_*$ denote ordinary derived direct image; $j_!$ is exact extension by zero [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement], and $Ri^!$ is the ambient right adjoint of $i_*$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], derived tensor $\otimes_A^L$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], and derived internal Hom $\mathscr H_T(U,V)=R\mathcal Hom_{A_T}(U,V)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Scheme inverse images on these categories are exact constant-coefficient inverse images [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. For $P\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ put $H=\mathscr H_S(P,Rs^!M)$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\theta_{s,P,M}:\mathscr H_X(Rs_!P,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rs_*H$$
characterized as follows. For every $C\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $u:C\to Rs_*H$, let $\widetilde u:s^*C\to H$ be its adjoint under $s^*\dashv Rs_*$. The tensor-adjoint of $\theta_{s,P,M}^{-1}\circ u$ is exactly
$$C\otimes_A^LRs_!P\xrightarrow{\pi_s}Rs_!(s^*C\otimes_A^LP)\xrightarrow{Rs_!(\widetilde u\otimes1)}Rs_!(H\otimes_A^LP)\xrightarrow{Rs_!\mathrm{ev}}Rs_!Rs^!M\xrightarrow{\varepsilon^!_{s,M}}M.$$
Here $\pi_s$ is the canonical projection isomorphism [lem-sf-etale-generic-immersion-projection] and $\varepsilon^!$ is the counit of $Rs_!\dashv Rs^!$. No boundedness or constructibility of $C,P,M$ is required.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom); agent tensor-Hom transposition of the closed/open immersion adjunctions, normalizing lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom by evaluation.

proof.text: For every scheme morphism $u$, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] gives the underived module adjunction $u^*=u^{-1}\dashv u_*$, with $u^{-1}$ additive and exact; on derived categories $u^*$ is applied termwise, since an exact functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Derived adjunction $s^*\dashv Rs_*$: let $C$ be a complex on $X$ and $H\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, and choose a K-injective resolution $H\to I$ [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Since $s^{-1}$ is an exact left adjoint of $s_*$, the termwise complex $s_*I$ is K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], and $Rs_*H=Q(s_*I)$ because a K-injective complex computes the total right derived functor of $Q\circ s_*$ [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. Hence $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S)}(s^*C,H)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(S)}(s^{-1}C,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(X)}(C,s_*I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(C,Rs_*H)$, the outer equalities by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] and the middle bijection on homotopy classes $f\mapsto s_*(f)\circ\eta_C$, with inverse $g\mapsto\varepsilon_I\circ s^{-1}(g)$, by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy](b). Each identification is natural in $C\in K(X)$, and both outer functors invert quasi-isomorphisms in $C$, so the bijection is natural in $C\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$; it is natural in $H$ by functoriality of K-injective resolutions. This is the canonical adjunction $s^*\dashv Rs_*$; its counit $\varepsilon^*_{s,H}$ is represented by the termwise counit $s^{-1}s_*I\to I$. Open factor: [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] gives $j_!\dashv j^{-1}=j^*$ on module sheaves, $j_!$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and $j^{-1}$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so both act termwise on derived categories. For $N\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ with K-injective resolution $N\to I$, the complex $j^{-1}I$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applied to the exact left adjoint $j_!$, and represents $j^*N$ since $j^{-1}$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms. The same three identifications [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy](b) give $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(j_!P',N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(U)}(P',j^*N)$ naturally, the derived pair $j_!\dashv j^*$. Closed factor: $i_*\dashv Ri^!$ by [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. Composing the derived open and closed adjunctions gives $Rs_!=j_!i_*\dashv Ri^!j^*=Rs^!$, with counit $\varepsilon^!_{s,M}$ the composite of the two counits.

proof.text: For every C, the closed symmetric-monoidal statement lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal gives a natural tensor-Hom bijection from maps C\to\mathscr H_X(Rs_!P,M) to maps C\otimes_A^LRs_!P\to M, with evaluation as its counit. The projection isomorphism lem-sf-etale-generic-immersion-projection rewrites the latter as maps Rs_!(s^*C\otimes_A^LP)\to M. The adjunction Rs_!\dashv Rs^! from step 1 rewrites these as maps s^*C\otimes_A^LP\to Rs^!M, and the same closed tensor-Hom bijection on S rewrites them as maps s^*C\to H=\mathscr H_S(P,Rs^!M). Thus the resulting bijection from Hom_X(C,\mathscr H_X(Rs_!P,M)) to Hom_S(s^*C,H) is natural in C.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), tensor-Hom transposition combined with the immersion projection formula

proof.text: The derived inverse-image/direct-image adjunction s^*\dashv Rs_* from step 1 identifies maps s^*C\to H with maps C\to Rs_*H. Composing this bijection with the natural bijection of step 2 gives, for every C, a bijection Hom_X(C,\mathscr H_X(Rs_!P,M))\cong Hom_X(C,Rs_*H), natural in C. Yoneda therefore defines a unique morphism \theta_{s,P,M}:\mathscr H_X(Rs_!P,M)\to Rs_*H whose postcomposition sends each map from C to the corresponding map under this bijection; since every component is bijective, \theta is an isomorphism. This defines \theta directly from the adjunction chain and does not invoke the unspecified isomorphism of lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), Yoneda construction from the tensor-adjunction chain

proof.text: Let u:C\to Rs_*H and let \widetilde u:s^*C\to H be its adjoint under s^*\dashv Rs_*. Tracing the inverse of the Yoneda bijection in step 3, and using the evaluation-counit clause of lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal, says that the tensor transpose of \theta_{s,P,M}^{-1}\circ u is exactly the composite $$C\otimes_A^LRs_!P\xrightarrow{\pi_s}Rs_!(s^*C\otimes_A^LP)\xrightarrow{Rs_!(\widetilde u\otimes1)}Rs_!(H\otimes_A^LP)\xrightarrow{Rs_!\mathrm{ev}}Rs_!Rs^!M\xrightarrow{\varepsilon^!_{s,M}}M.$$ Every arrow is the corresponding map in the adjunction chain, so its naturality in C, P and M follows from naturality of the closed tensor-Hom bijections, the projection isomorphism, the two adjunctions, evaluation, and the counit; no boundedness or constructibility hypothesis is introduced.
